[0] everyday_reading (E): In maths, a = b = 0 states that all three quantities are equal at once, in any reading order. In Java the = operators group right to left: b = 0 runs first, and its value 0 is then assigned to a.
[1] misconception (M) -> AssignmentNotExpression: wrong rule: an assignment cannot be used inside a larger expression. Right rule: An assignment is an expression whose value is the value assigned, so (x = v) both stores v in x and gives v.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> AssignmentNotExpression: Points to LT (the rightmost assignment runs first, and its value feeds the next one to its left). Applied unevenly, a student evaluates a = b first and gives a the old value of b. (here mixing in: "an assignment cannot be used inside a larger expression")

[0] names_the_element (N): Chained assignment: several = in one expression (a = b = c = 0) that assigns one value to several variables.
[1] states_the_rule (S): = is right-associative, and an assignment expression has the value that was stored, so a = b = 0 means a = (b = 0). Every target must be a variable whose type accepts the value.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): The innermost (rightmost) assignment runs first: evaluate 0, store it in b, and that assignment's value 0 is then stored in a.
[1] output_prediction (OP): The whole expression's value is the value assigned. With int i and double d, d = i = 5 stores 5 in i and 5.0 in d.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): Every variable in the chain changes, right to left, to the same value (converted to its own type).

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): A chain works only because an assignment is itself an expression whose value is the value stored, so it can be the right side of another =.
[1] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Initializing several counters or accumulators to the same starting value in one line (sum = count = 0).

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> AssignmentNotExpression: Reordering targets with different types can break the chain: d = i = 5 compiles, but i = d = 5 does not, because the double value of d = 5 cannot go into int i.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use a chain only to give several variables of the same type one simple starting value. Avoid chains inside conditions or with expressions that have side effects.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Every value in the chain must be assignable to the next target's type. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: A chain passing through a wider type into a narrower one (int i; double d; i = d = 2.5;): 'possible lossy conversion'.
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: int a = b = 0; declares only a; b must already exist. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: Using the chain in a declaration with an undeclared inner variable: 'cannot find symbol b'.

wrong: A read and a test cannot be combined, so while ((x = read()) != end) is not allowed. | right: while ((x = read()) != end) reads a value into x and tests that same value in one expression.
An assignment such as x = y is treated as an expression: it assigns the value of y to x and evaluates to that value.
